literal: Therefore the Empress Dowager deeply favored Teng and the other four men and all received favored appointments.
idiomatic: The Empress Dowager therefore deeply favored Teng and the other three and richly rewarded them.

literal: Zhong, because many slandered him, feared he could not escape disaster and wished to return to the capital to rescue himself.
idiomatic: Many slandered Zhong; fearing ruin, he begged to return to the capital to save himself.

literal: The Empress Dowager did not permit it.
idiomatic: The Empress Dowager refused.

literal: In the fourth month of the second year he was made Right Vice Director of the Secretariat and added Palace Attendant, general as before.
idiomatic: In the second year, fourth month, he became Right Vice Director and Attendant, retaining his generalship.

literal: In the third month of the first year of Shengui he was again Honored Companion of the First Rank.
idiomatic: In Shengui year one, third month, he was again Honored Companion.

literal: He fell ill and did not assume the post.
idiomatic: He fell ill before he could take the post.

literal: Seeing Pei and Guo as apparitions, he knew he must die; he first memorialized to adopt his late younger brother's second son, Registrar Yongchao of the Ministry of Works, as his heir and begged him as legitimate son.
idiomatic: Haunted by visions of Pei and Guo, he knew death was near; he memorialized to adopt his late brother's second son Yongchao, a registrar of Works, as heir.

literal: The Empress Dowager permitted it.
idiomatic: The Empress Dowager consented.

literal: At death he was posthumously made Minister of Works.
idiomatic: At his death he was posthumously made Minister of Works.

literal: The relevant offices memorialized; Vice Director of the Imperial Ancestral Temple Yuan Duan argued, "According to the posthumous canon, rigid and upright in principle is called Martial; one who relies on power and acts wantonly is called Violent-Brutal—the posthumous name should be Duke Martial Violent-Brutal.
idiomatic: The bureaus memorialized; Vice Director Yuan Duan argued, "By the posthumous canon, rigid uprightness is Martial; bullying power is Violent—the name should be Martial Violent Duke.

literal: Director Yuan Xiuyi argued, "Zhong gave his heart to serve above and cut down fierce rebels.
idiomatic: Director Yuan Xiuyi argued, "Zhong served with all his heart and cut down traitors.

literal: By the posthumous canon, removing falsehood and settling the straight is Martial; diligent service night and day is Reverent—the posthumous name should be Duke Martial Reverent.
idiomatic: By canon, rooting out falsehood is Martial; tireless service is Reverent—the name should be Martial Reverent Duke.

literal: The two directors differed.
idiomatic: The two directors disagreed.

literal: The Empress Dowager ordered that the senior director's argument be followed.
idiomatic: The Empress Dowager followed the senior director.

literal: Zhong by nature was much obstructive and jealous, did not associate with those who surpassed him, and only with Direct Attendant Zhang Chuhuan and Thousand-Ox Guard Yang Baoyuan had bonds like severed metal.
idiomatic: Zhong was jealous and would not befriend his betters; only Direct Attendant Zhang Chuhuan and Thousand-Ox Guard Yang Baoyuan were his sworn brothers.

literal: Li Shizhe sought favor from Zhong and privately used gold and silk to buy Chuhuan and Baoyuan; the two spoke for him and he was thereupon favored and drawn into the inner circle.
idiomatic: Li Shizhe courted Zhong, bribing Chuhuan and Baoyuan with gold and silk; they spoke for him and he became Zhong's confidant.

literal: Zhong's monopolizing power and blind advancement in Chongxun—all were Shizhe's schemes.
idiomatic: Zhong's seizure of power and blind promotions at Chongxun were Shizhe's doing.

literal: Zhong's younger brother Jing, original name Bainian.
idiomatic: Zhong's younger brother Jing had originally been named Bainian.

literal: After Zhong died he became Martial Guard General.
idiomatic: After Zhong's death he became Martial Guard General.

literal: He plotted to depose Yuan Cha; Cha demoted him to Garrison Commander of Huaihuang.
idiomatic: He plotted to depose Yuan Cha; Cha sent him to Garrison Commander of Huaihuang.

literal: When the Rouran lord Anagui rebelled, the garrison men asked for grain and Jing did not supply it.
idiomatic: When Rouran lord Anagui rebelled, the garrison begged grain; Jing refused.

literal: The garrison men then seized and bound Jing and his wife, confined them in a separate room, stripped them all of clothing, made Jing wear a fur coat and his wife wear an old crimson banner jacket, and insulted them thus.
idiomatic: The garrison seized Jing and his wife, stripped them, clothed him in furs and her in a tattered crimson banner-coat, and shamed them so.

literal: After more than a month they killed them.
idiomatic: After a month they killed them both.

literal: Jing's younger brother Guo was stern, resolute, upright, and bright, with the bearing of father and elder brother.
idiomatic: Jing's younger brother Guo was stern, upright, and bright, in the mold of father and brother.

literal: He served as Inspector of Shuo, Hua, Bing, and Heng, and was granted Viscount of Wucheng.
idiomatic: He held Shuo, Hua, Bing, and Heng and was made Viscount of Wucheng.

literal: Guo's younger brother Jin.
idiomatic: Guo's younger brother was Jin.

literal: Jin, style name Zhongkui, had considerable military talent; he was Garrison Commander of Woye and granted Viscount of Fuchang.
idiomatic: Jin, styled Zhongkui, was skilled in war; he commanded Woye and was Viscount of Fuchang.

literal: Xuanwu took his daughter as empress and enfeoffed Jin Duke of Taiyuan; his wife Lady Liu was made Lady of Zhangwu.
idiomatic: Xuanwu made his daughter empress, enfeoffed Jin Duke of Taiyuan, and made his wife Lady Liu Lady of Zhangwu.

literal: Later he was General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Dingzhou.
idiomatic: He later became General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Dingzhou.

literal: At death he was posthumously made Minister of Works and given the posthumous title Duke Gongzhuang.
idiomatic: At his death he was posthumously Minister of Works with the posthumous name Duke Gongzhuang.

literal: From Lidi to Jin, for generations they were noble and grand—one empress, four posthumous dukes, three Generals of the Guards, two Directors of the Secretariat, three founding dukes.
idiomatic: From Lidi to Jin the house flourished for generations—one empress, four posthumous dukes, three Guard generals, two Secretariat directors, three founding dukes.

literal: Though Jin was father of the empress, because Empress Shun died early he never reached chief counselor.
idiomatic: Though Jin was the empress's father, Empress Shun's early death kept him from the highest office.

literal: His son Hui, style name Xuanming, was a son of the later wife.
idiomatic: His son Hui, styled Xuanming, was born of the later wife.

literal: In youth he had spirit and capacity.
idiomatic: Young he showed spirit and capacity.

literal: He inherited the title and was Inspector of Fenzhou.
idiomatic: He inherited the fief and became Inspector of Fenzhou.

literal: Hui was skilled at winning men and was favored by Erzhu Rong, who gave his daughter to Rong's son Changru.
idiomatic: Hui knew how to win hearts; Erzhu Rong favored him and gave him his daughter for son Changru.

literal: He served as Palace Attendant and Mayor of Henan.
idiomatic: He served as Palace Attendant and Mayor of Henan.

literal: Later he was concurrently Vice Director of the Secretariat and Commissioner of the Southeastern Circuit, and with Qi Shenwu subdued Yang Kan in Yanzhou.
idiomatic: He later became Vice Director and Southeastern Commissioner and with Qi Shenwu crushed Yang Kan in Yanzhou.

literal: When Yuan Hao entered Luoyang he was killed.
idiomatic: When Yuan Hao took Luoyang, Hui was killed.

literal: Jin's younger brother Tian'en was Inner Steward and Governor of Liaoxi.
idiomatic: Jin's younger brother Tian'en was Inner Steward and Governor of Liaoxi.

literal: Posthumously made General Who Pacifies the East and Inspector of Yanzhou.
idiomatic: He was posthumously General Who Pacifies the East and Inspector of Yanzhou.

literal: Tian'en's son Rensheng was Grand Palace Counselor.
idiomatic: Tian'en's son Rensheng was Grand Palace Counselor.

literal: Rensheng's son Anding was Administrator of Pingyuan and Chief Commandant of Gaoping.
idiomatic: Rensheng's son Anding was Administrator of Pingyuan and Chief Commandant of Gaoping.

literal: Anding's son Ziti was Governor of Longxi and Baron of Maoping.
idiomatic: Anding's son Ziti was Governor of Longxi and Baron of Maoping.

literal: In the second year of Zhou's Baoding, because son Jin's merit was illustrious, he was posthumously made Grand Guardian and Duke of Jianping.
idiomatic: In Zhou Baoding year two, for son Jin's merit, Ziti's line was posthumously made Grand Guardian and Duke of Jianping.

literal: Jin, style name Sijing, childhood name Juyin.
idiomatic: Jin, styled Sijing, childhood name Juyin.

literal: Deep and reserved with discernment, he glanced at classics and histories and especially loved Sunzi's Art of War.
idiomatic: Deep, reserved, and discerning, he skimmed the classics and especially loved Sunzi's Art of War.

literal: Living in seclusion he had no wish to advance in office.
idiomatic: In retirement he had no wish for office.

literal: When some urged him, Jin said, "Posts of prefecture and commandery the ancients despised; the tripod of state one must await the right time.
idiomatic: When urged to serve, Jin said, "Prefectures and commanderies ancients scorned; the highest offices wait on the hour.

literal: " Grand Preceptor Yuan Tianmu saw him and sighed, "Material for a king's assistant.
idiomatic: Grand Preceptor Yuan Tianmu saw him and sighed, "A king's right hand.

literal: " When Poliuhan Baling first raised turmoil on the northern border and drew the Rouran as allies, the Grand Commissioner Yuan Zuan campaigned against him.
idiomatic: When Poliuhan Baling first rebelled in the north and called in the Rouran, Commissioner Yuan Zuan marched against him.

literal: Long having heard Jin's name, he recruited him as Registrar of Armor and he followed the army north.
idiomatic: Zuan had long heard of Jin and made him Armor Registrar on the northern campaign.

literal: The Rouran fled beyond the passes; Zuan ordered Jin to pursue them—seventeen battles in all—and all their masses surrendered.
idiomatic: The Rouran fled the border; Zuan sent Jin after them; seventeen battles later all had submitted.

literal: Later he led light cavalry beyond the passes to scout the enemy; several thousand Tiele horsemen suddenly arrived.
idiomatic: Later he led light horse beyond the passes to scout; thousands of Tiele horsemen fell upon him.

literal: Jin, seeing his force too few to match them, scattered his riders and hid them in thickets.
idiomatic: Outnumbered, Jin scattered his riders into the brush.

literal: He also sent men up the mountain to signal as if dividing the army.
idiomatic: He sent men up the hills to signal as though deploying divisions.

literal: The enemy saw it; though they suspected an ambush, trusting their numbers they did not worry and pressed upon Jin.
idiomatic: The enemy saw this; though they feared ambush, their numbers made them bold and they pressed Jin.

literal: His usual mounts were one bay and one piebald the enemy already knew; he therefore had two men each ride one horse and burst through the array.
idiomatic: His usual mounts were a bay and a piebald the enemy knew; he set two men on those horses to break the line.

literal: The enemy thought it was Jin and strove to pursue.
idiomatic: The foe took them for Jin and gave chase.

literal: He then led the remaining troops to strike their pursuing horsemen.
idiomatic: Jin then struck the pursuers with his remnant force.

literal: The enemy fled and he was thus able to enter the passes.
idiomatic: They fled and he re-entered the passes.

literal: In the fourth year of Zhengguang, Commissioner Prince Yuan Shen of Guangyang marched north; he recruited Jin as Registrar of the Long Stream.
idiomatic: In Zhengguang year four Prince Yuan Shen of Guangyang marched north and took Jin as Long Stream Registrar.

literal: He treated him with special courtesy and had his heir Fotuo bow to him.
idiomatic: Shen honored him specially and had his heir Fotuo perform obeisance.

literal: He then with Guangyang broke the bandit chief Hulu Yegulu and others.
idiomatic: With Guangyang he broke the bandit chief Hulu Yegulu and his fellows.

literal: Jin asked to ride ahead and persuade them.
idiomatic: Jin asked to ride ahead and win them by persuasion.

literal: Jin also understood the languages of many states; he entered the enemy camp alone on one horse, showed grace and trust, and thereupon chieftains of the western Tiele such as Yelie He, more than thirty thousand households, all submitted and came south in succession.
idiomatic: Jin knew many tongues; alone he rode into the enemy camp, showed grace and faith, and western Tiele chiefs including Yelie He—thirty thousand households—submitted and moved south.

literal: Guangyang with Jin went to Xige Ridge to welcome them.
idiomatic: Guangyang and Jin met them at Xige Ridge.

literal: Jin said, "Baling's troops are not few; hearing that Yelie He and others have submitted, he is sure to come to intercept.
idiomatic: Jin said, "Baling's host is large; hearing of Yelie He's submission, he will intercept.

literal: If he first holds the defiles, we cannot contend for advantage.
idiomatic: If he seizes the passes first, we cannot fight him on equal ground.

literal: Now use Yelie He and the rest as bait—he will surely come to plunder in rivalry; then set an ambush and wait, and you will break him as easily as turning the palm.
idiomatic: Use Yelie He as bait; Baling will rush to plunder; then ambush him and break him in the palm of your hand.

literal: Guangyang approved his plan.
idiomatic: Guangyang agreed.

literal: Baling indeed came to intercept; he broke Yelie He on the ridge and all his following perished.
idiomatic: Baling came to intercept, shattered Yelie He on the ridge, and destroyed his following.

literal: Jin's ambush troops rose; the bandits were greatly defeated and he gathered and broke all of Yelie He's people.
idiomatic: Jin's ambush rose; the rebels were routed and he recovered Yelie He's people.

literal: In the first year of Xiaochang he again followed Prince of Guangyang to campaign against Xianyu Xiuli.
idiomatic: In Xiaochang year one he again followed Guangyang against Xianyu Xiuli.

literal: The army halted at White Bull Fighting Camp.
idiomatic: The army camped at White Bull Fighting Camp.

literal: When Prince Zhangwu was killed by Xiuli, the army stopped at Zhongshan.
idiomatic: Prince Zhangwu fell to Xiuli; the army halted at Zhongshan.

literal: Palace Attendant Yuan Yan declared to Empress Dowager Ling, "Guangyang lingers without advancing, sitting and plotting unseemly aims.
idiomatic: Attendant Yuan Yan told Empress Dowager Ling, "Guangyang stalls and plots beyond his station.

literal: Moreover there is Yu Jin, whose stratagems surpass others and who is his chief planner—I fear he is not Your Majesty's pure servant.
idiomatic: His chief planner Yu Jin exceeds ordinary wit—I fear he is no loyal servant of Your Majesty.

literal: " The Empress Dowager decreed a placard set outside the gate of the Ministry of the Imperial Secretariat offering a heavy reward to whoever captured Jin.
idiomatic: The Empress Dowager posted a placard at the Secretariat gate offering a rich reward for Jin's capture.

literal: Jin heard of it and asked to go to the palace and lay bare his heart; Guangyang permitted it.
idiomatic: Jin heard and asked to go to court and lay bare his heart; Guangyang consented.

literal: Jin then came beneath the placard and said, "I know this man.
idiomatic: Jin came to the placard and said, "I know this man.

literal: The crowd together questioned him; Jin said:
idiomatic: The crowd pressed him; Jin said:

literal: "I am he.
idiomatic: "I am he.

literal: The relevant offices reported it.
idiomatic: The officers reported it.

literal: The Empress Dowager saw him and was greatly angry.
idiomatic: The Empress Dowager received him in great anger.

literal: Jin fully set forth Guangyang's loyal intent and together stated the reason for halting the army.
idiomatic: Jin laid out Guangyang's loyalty and the army's reasons for halting.

literal: The Empress Dowager then released him.
idiomatic: The Empress Dowager spared him.

literal: Later he followed Erzhu Tian Guang in battle with Qi Shenwu at Hanling Mountain; Tian Guang was defeated and Jin then entered the passes.
idiomatic: Later he followed Erzhu Tian Guang against Qi Shenwu at Hanling; Tian Guang lost and Jin entered the passes.

literal: When Zhou Wendi came to Xiazhou he made Jin Grand Defender of the City and Concurrent Chief Administrator of Xiazhou.
idiomatic: When Zhou Wendi came to Xiazhou he made Jin Grand Defender and Concurrent Administrator.

literal: When Heba Yue was killed, Wendi went to Pingliang.
idiomatic: When Heba Yue was murdered, Wendi went to Pingliang.

literal: Jin spoke to Wendi, "Guanzhong is the old capital of Qin and Han, anciently called the Storehouse of Heaven.
idiomatic: Jin told Wendi, "Guanzhong was Qin and Han's capital, the ancient Storehouse of Heaven.

literal: If we now hold its strategic points and gather heroes, we may well watch the times change.
idiomatic: Hold its passes and gather heroes and we can read the times.

literal: Moreover the Son of Heaven is in Luoyang, pressed by a host of villains.
idiomatic: The Son of Heaven sits in Luoyang, harried by villains.

literal: I beg to establish the capital in the west of the passes, then hold the Son of Heaven and command the feudal lords—a chance once in a thousand years.
idiomatic: Move the capital west of the passes, hold the Son of Heaven, and command the lords—a chance once in a millennium.

literal: Wendi was greatly pleased.
idiomatic: Wendi was delighted.

literal: It happened that an edict recalled Jin as Grand Commander Within the Passes; Jin thereupon advanced the plan to establish the capital in Guanzhong.
idiomatic: An edict recalled him as Grand Commander Within the Passes; Jin advanced the Guanzhong capital plan.

literal: When the Wei Emperor moved west he still followed Wendi in the campaign for Tong Pass, broke Huiluo city, was appointed Inspector of Beiyong, and advanced to Duke of Lantian.
idiomatic: When the Wei Emperor moved west he followed Wendi to Tong Pass, took Huiluo, became Inspector of Beiyong, and was made Duke of Lantian.

literal: In the third year of Datong, the great army campaigned east; as vanguard he advanced and took Hongnong and captured Eastern Wei Inspector of Shaan Li Huibo.
idiomatic: In Datong year three, as eastern vanguard he took Hongnong and captured Eastern Wei Inspector of Shaan Li Huibo.

literal: Shenwu came to Shayuan; Jin fought fiercely and was advanced to Duke of Changshan.
idiomatic: Shenwu came to Shayuan; Jin fought hard and was advanced Duke of Changshan.

literal: He again followed in the battle at Heqiao and was appointed Chief Clerk of the Grand Chancellor's Office and Concurrent Director of the Grand Commissioner of the Imperial Secretariat.
idiomatic: He fought at Heqiao and became Chief Clerk to the Grand Chancellor and Concurrent Director of the Grand Commissioner's Secretariat.
